genes.name: symmetric
genes.hypothesis: A symmetric h (h_i = h_(n-1-i)) has a symmetric overlap profile c_s = c_(-s), and the coarse profile of all three published top solutions is symmetric. Restricting the search to symmetric functions halves the dimension and the number of distinct shifts, so the descent converges faster at short budgets, at the price of excluding the asymmetric fine structure that the published optima do have.
genes.predicted: small gain at 5-second budgets; neutral or a loss at long ones
genes.author: seed

genes.name: coarse_to_fine
genes.hypothesis: The score is unchanged when every height is repeated, and a descent step on n / coarse_factor steps is coarse_factor times cheaper. Spending the first part of the budget on a coarse grid finds the global shape (the basin) in fewer CPU seconds, and the fine grid only has to add detail.
genes.predicted: -1e-3 to -5e-3 in score at n >= 512 for 5-second budgets
genes.author: seed

genes.name: lp_polish
genes.hypothesis: The log-sum-exp surrogate stops short of a true minimax point by about log(number of active shifts) / beta. At an optimum hundreds of shifts are nearly tied (730 of 2047 within 1e-6 of the maximum in the second-best published solution), which is the situation a linear program over the near-maximal shifts solves exactly; sequential LP in a trust box should equalise the plateau and close the gap.
genes.predicted: -1e-4 to -1e-3 in score at n <= 512; a loss at n = 1024 in 5 seconds, where each LP is slow
genes.author: seed

genes.name: init_noise
genes.hypothesis: Standard deviation of the Gaussian noise added to the flat start h = 1/2 before projection; the only source of diversity between seeds.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: beta0
genes.hypothesis: Initial sharpness of the log-sum-exp surrogate (score units, the score is about 0.38). Low values look at the whole overlap profile and move the shape; high values only flatten the peaks.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: beta_growth
genes.hypothesis: Factor by which the sharpness grows after every stage; faster growth commits to a basin sooner.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: stage_iters
genes.hypothesis: Gradient evaluations per stage before the sharpness is raised; more lets each stage converge, fewer reaches the sharp end of the schedule within the budget.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: step0
genes.hypothesis: Initial projected-gradient step, as the largest change of any height; it adapts afterwards, so it mainly matters right after each sharpness increase.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: coarse_factor
genes.hypothesis: The coarse grid has n / coarse_factor steps; coarser is cheaper but may decide on a shape that the fine grid cannot repair.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: coarse_fraction
genes.hypothesis: Share of the descent budget spent on the coarse grid.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: polish_fraction
genes.hypothesis: Share of the budget kept back for the LP polish at the end.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: polish_window
genes.hypothesis: Shifts within this relative distance of the maximum enter the LP; too narrow and a step runs into shifts the LP did not see, too wide and each LP is slow.
genes.author: seed

genes.name: polish_radius
genes.hypothesis: Initial half-width of the LP trust box, in units of height; it adapts afterwards.
genes.author: seed
